title: Typeform vs Formbricks
comparison_markdown:
# Typeform vs Formbricks (2026)

## Overview
Typeform and Formbricks are both online form and survey builders that help businesses and individuals collect data and feedback from their audience. This comparison is beneficial for those who want to switch from a proprietary, cloud-based solution to a self-hosted, open-source alternative, with a core use case of creating custom forms and surveys. The key reason someone would switch is to have full control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Typeform offers a free plan and paid plans starting at $25/month, while Formbricks is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Formbricks allows users to have full control over their data, while Typeform stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Typeform has a more user-friendly interface and is easier to set up, while Formbricks requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Formbricks can be more scalable than Typeform since it can be self-hosted on a user's own server.
* Integration: Typeform has a more extensive library of integrations with third-party services, including popular marketing and CRM tools, while Formbricks has limited integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Typeform | Formbricks |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $25-$83/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $1.25-$4.15 per user per month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $1.25-$4.15 per user per month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Typeform:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Extensive library of integrations
* User-friendly interface
* Scalable
* Limited control over data
**Formbricks:**
* Self-hosted and open-source
* Full control over data
* Scalable
* Free
* Limited integrations and technical support

## When to Choose Each
Typeform is suitable for small to medium-sized businesses or individuals who want a user-friendly and easy-to-set-up form builder with a wide range of integrations. It is ideal for those who prioritize ease of use and are willing to compromise on data control. Formbricks, on the other hand, is suitable for larger organizations or technical teams that require full control over their data and are willing to invest time in setting up and maintaining their own server.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Formbricks instance on your own server.
3. Use the Formbricks import tool to migrate your Typeform data.
4. Configure any additional settings or integrations as needed.
5. Test your forms and surveys to ensure they are working as expected.

## Our Take
Formbricks is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited technical support and integrations. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Formbricks requires a certain level of technical expertise to set up and maintain. However, for teams that value data control and are willing to invest time in setting up and maintaining their own server, Formbricks is a viable alternative to Typeform.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams with basic form-building needs who do not require integrations with third-party services.
* Technical teams with experience in self-hosting and maintaining their own servers.
* Organizations with strict data control requirements.
* Businesses with limited budgets who want a free, self-hosted solution.
* Individuals who want full control over their data and are willing to invest time in setting up and maintaining their own server.

## FAQ
### What is the main difference between Typeform and Formbricks?
The main difference is that Typeform is a proprietary, cloud-based solution, while Formbricks is a self-hosted, open-source alternative.
### Can I use Formbricks for free?
Yes, Formbricks is free and self-hosted, meaning you can use it without paying any subscription fees.
### Is Formbricks suitable for large organizations?
Formbricks can be suitable for larger organizations, but it requires a certain level of technical expertise to set up and maintain.
### Can I migrate my Typeform data to Formbricks?
Yes, you can export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format and import it into Formbricks using the Formbricks import tool.
### Does Formbricks have integrations with popular marketing tools?
Not yet, Formbricks has limited integrations with third-party services, but it is actively developing new integrations.

# Miro vs Excalidraw

## Overview

Online collaborative whiteboard platform. is a popular proprietary tool in the design space. Excalidraw is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Miro costs Free / $8-$16/user/month; Excalidraw is Free
- **License**: Miro is Proprietary; Excalidraw is MIT
- **Data ownership**: Excalidraw can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Excalidraw eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Excalidraw has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Miro | Excalidraw |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $8-$16/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Miro

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Excalidraw

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [excalidraw/excalidraw](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw) * ~90k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Miro if:** Miro is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Excalidraw if:** Excalidraw is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Miro in its standard export format, review Excalidraw import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Excalidraw is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Miro tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Excalidraw instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Miro, switching to self-hosted Excalidraw will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Miro until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Miro paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Excalidraw free to use?
Yes. Excalidraw is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Miro to Excalidraw?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Miro data, follow the Excalidraw import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Excalidraw get regular updates?
Yes. Excalidraw has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Excalidraw without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Excalidraw development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Miro](https://miro.com) and [Excalidraw](https://excalidraw.com) before making decisions.*

Both tools cater to developers and businesses looking to streamline their workflow and improve application performance. * Cost: Netlify offers a range of pricing plans, including a free plan, while Coolify is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Coolify allows users to retain full ownership of their data, while Netlify stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Netlify is generally easier to set up, with a more user-friendly interface, while Coolify requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Netlify offers automatic scaling, while Coolify requires manual configuration.
* Feature difference: Netlify offers built-in support for serverless functions, while Coolify relies on third-party integrations.

| Aspect | Netlify | Coolify |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $19-$99/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |

| Per-user cost at 200 users | $99-$495/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Netlify
* Easy to set up and use
* Automatic scaling and performance optimization
* Built-in support for serverless functions
* Large community and extensive documentation
* Limited control over data and infrastructure
### Coolify
* Free and self-hosted
* Full control over data and infrastructure
* Highly customizable and extensible
* Apache 2.0 license
* Steeper learning curve and more complex setup

## When to Choose Each
Netlify is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that prioritize ease of use and automatic scaling. It's ideal for teams that don't require fine-grained control over their infrastructure and are willing to pay for the convenience. Coolify, on the other hand, is suitable for larger teams or enterprises that require full control over their data and infrastructure. It's also a good choice for teams with advanced technical expertise and a need for high customization.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Netlify site using the Netlify CLI or the web interface.
2. Set up a Coolify instance on your own server or virtual machine.
3. Use the Coolify import tool to migrate your site data and configuration.
4. Configure any additional settings or integrations as needed.
5. Test your site thoroughly to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Coolify is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the polish and ease of use that Netlify offers. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Coolify requires manual configuration of scaling and performance optimization, which can be time-consuming and error-prone. However, for teams that require full control over their data and infrastructure, Coolify is a compelling alternative to Netlify, and we recommend considering it for teams with advanced technical expertise.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams that require full control over their data and infrastructure
* Medium-sized teams that need high customization and extensibility
* Large enterprises with advanced technical expertise
* Teams that don't require automatic scaling and performance optimization
* Developers who prioritize open-source software and community involvement

## FAQ
### What is the main difference between Netlify and Coolify?
The main difference is that Netlify is a proprietary, cloud-based platform, while Coolify is free and self-hosted.
### Can I use Coolify for free?
Yes, Coolify is free and self-hosted, which means you can use it without paying any licensing fees.
### Is Coolify suitable for small teams?
Coolify can be suitable for small teams, but it may require more technical expertise and setup effort compared to Netlify.
### Can I migrate my Netlify site to Coolify?
Yes, you can migrate your Netlify site to Coolify using the Coolify import tool and following the migration path outlined above.
### Is Coolify production-ready?
Not yet, Coolify is still in development and lacks some of the polish and ease of use that Netlify offers.

title: Shopify vs WooCommerce
comparison_markdown:
# Shopify vs WooCommerce (2026)

## Overview
Shopify and WooCommerce are two popular e-commerce platforms that enable businesses to create online stores and sell products. This comparison is beneficial for entrepreneurs, small business owners, and e-commerce teams who want to choose the best platform for their online store. The core use case for both tools is to provide a scalable and secure e-commerce solution, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Shopify has a monthly subscription fee, while WooCommerce is free to download and use.
* Data ownership: WooCommerce provides full data ownership, while Shopify has some limitations on data export and usage.
* Setup complexity: Shopify has a more streamlined setup process, while WooCommerce requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Both platforms are scalable, but WooCommerce requires more manual configuration to handle high traffic and sales volumes.
* Payment gateway integration: Shopify has a built-in payment gateway, while WooCommerce requires third-party payment gateway integrations, such as Stripe or PayPal.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Shopify | WooCommerce |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $29-$299+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $29-$49/month (Basic Shopify plan) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $299-$499+/month (Advanced Shopify plan) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Shopify:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Streamlined payment processing
* 24/7 customer support
* Limited control over data and customization
* Transaction fees apply
**WooCommerce:**
* Free to download and use
* Full control over data and customization
* Scalable and flexible
* Requires technical expertise to set up and manage
* Limited customer support

## When to Choose Each
Shopify is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses that want a streamlined e-commerce solution with minimal setup and maintenance requirements. It's ideal for teams with limited technical expertise who want to focus on sales and marketing. WooCommerce, on the other hand, is suitable for larger businesses or enterprises that require more control over their e-commerce platform and data. It's ideal for teams with technical expertise who want to customize and scale their online store.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Shopify data in CSV format using the Shopify export tool.
2. Install and set up WooCommerce on your self-hosted WordPress site.
3. Use the WooCommerce import tool to import your Shopify data, including products, customers, and orders.
4. Configure your payment gateways and shipping options in WooCommerce.
5. Test your WooCommerce site to ensure a smooth transition.

## Our Take
WooCommerce is a production-ready e-commerce platform for most users, offering a high degree of customization and control over data. However, one technical limitation worth knowing is that WooCommerce requires a self-hosted WordPress site, which can add complexity to setup and maintenance. We recommend switching to WooCommerce if you're a medium-sized business or enterprise that wants more control over your e-commerce platform and data, but if you're a small business with limited technical expertise, Shopify may still be the better choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with technical expertise who want more control over their e-commerce platform
* Medium-sized businesses that require customization and scalability
* Enterprises with large sales volumes and complex product catalogs
* Businesses that want to avoid transaction fees and have full control over their data
* Teams with in-house development resources who want to customize and extend their e-commerce platform

## FAQ
### Can I use WooCommerce with any WordPress theme?
Yes, WooCommerce is compatible with most WordPress themes, but some themes may require additional configuration or customization to work seamlessly with WooCommerce.
### Is Shopify more secure than WooCommerce?
Both Shopify and WooCommerce have robust security features, but Shopify has a more streamlined security setup process, while WooCommerce requires more manual configuration.
### Can I migrate my Shopify data to WooCommerce?
Yes, you can export your Shopify data in CSV format and import it into WooCommerce using the WooCommerce import tool.
### Does WooCommerce have built-in payment processing?
No, WooCommerce requires third-party payment gateway integrations, such as Stripe or PayPal.
### Is WooCommerce free to use?
Yes, WooCommerce is free to download and use, but you'll need to pay for hosting and any additional extensions or themes you want to use.
